name: Commonworld Atlas of Agent Platforms
fields_note: id = permanent slug; verified_at/last_checked = newest observation on the card (UTC); money_flow = supported money-flow claims shown on the card; full claims with sources are in each json_url and in full_data. Primary overview mode: overview.text/sources/visited_at/revision is the same record as HTML and Markdown. Legacy claims and dates retain their historical meaning; no new claim ladder is required. Drafts are not release-ready.

platforms.name: 402atlas
platforms.summary: 402atlas is an independent paid-test map of x402 services (each listed service bought with real USDC from a public audit wallet) plus an on-chain market report on real vs. inflated x402 volume.

money_flow.statement: Report estimate: real economic demand ~$145–390k/month (run-rate × (1−wash%), analysis cutoff 2026-06-14); 6 of top-10 buyers traced to one self-funded loop on 2026-06-14.

overview.text: 402atlas presents a separate paid-test directory for x402 services on Base. It says it tests services with USDC and publishes responses, on-chain receipts and corrections. The site offers a free onboarding report and catalogue alongside a paid dataset API. Its footer dates the saved paid tests to 17 November 2026 and liveness rechecks to 18 November. These are its own testing claims, not tests or endorsements by Commonworld Atlas.

platforms.name: ACP + OpenAI Instant Checkout
platforms.summary: Open specification (maintained by OpenAI and Stripe) for buyers, their AI agents and merchants to complete purchases; homepage agenticcommerce.dev.

overview.text: Agentic Commerce Protocol is a beta interaction model and open standard for purchases between buyers, their AI agents and businesses, maintained by OpenAI and Stripe. Its public repository provides the specification, documentation, examples, a changelog and contribution guidance under Apache 2.0. It is distinct from Virtuals' Agent Commerce Protocol.

platforms.name: Agent402
platforms.summary: Pay-per-call tool hub for AI agents: 500+ metered tools, models and reports paid per request over x402 or MPP without signup or API keys, plus an open directory of indexed x402 sellers with their tools and settlement networks.

overview.text: Agent402 presents paid tools, a model gateway, outside-seller discovery and a router that buys answers from those sellers. It advertises multi-network x402, MPP on Tempo and proof-of-work access for selected pure-CPU tools, not free access to models, browsers or all third-party services. Pricing separates tool calls from $0.001, fixed model tiers and request-specific metered quotes. Exact-payment and usage-based clients can settle differently. x402 is described as settling after answer generation; upfront Tempo failures become refund debts. A disconnect after settlement may leave a charge without the answer, subject to refund review, not universal automatic refunds. Signed receipts concern payment records rather than answer quality. First-party counters and the whole-ecosystem visualization have different scopes and do not establish independent users or reliable completion. Card reports and $5/month monitors are separate offers. Model providers and routing sellers process request data; stored ledgers and wallet-keyed memory qualify no-account marketing.

platforms.name: AgentCard
platforms.summary: Lets an AI agent pay online with a one-time-use card linked to the user's own card, with spending limits and purchase tracking; the operator says Mastercard holders pay through Mastercard Agent Pay.

overview.text: AgentCard presents online agent purchases using an owner's existing funding card, with spending limits, purchase tracking and a one-use card per purchase. It advertises Mastercard Agent Pay and Verifiable Intent support, with passkey approval of merchant/amount requests; partnership and safety statements are publisher claims rather than independent verification. Setup includes magic-link sign-in, funding-card selection, an agent email and wallet, and one identity check before first spend. Thirty-second and no-approval-queue marketing does not guarantee identity approval or card eligibility. Other cards are advertised but their route is not established here. No subscription and pay-for-purchases wording is not a universal no-fee promise or refund policy. Rotating merchant names, purchases and prices are illustrations, not a verified acceptance list, current offers or completed transactions.

platforms.name: Agentic.Market
platforms.summary: Coinbase-operated storefront/directory of x402-enabled services agents can discover and pay per request in USDC.

overview.text: Agentic Market presents x402 service discovery with payment charts, a services leaderboard, featured bundles and a catalogue of services, endpoints and bundles. It offers category, network and verification filters, an agent skill and seller endpoint validation. The footer identifies Coinbase as the operator and says the marketplace is not an official x402 Foundation product. Prices, rankings and statistics are site-reported.

platforms.name: AgenticMarket (MCP)
platforms.summary: Directory and gateway of verified MCP servers, agent skills and model benchmarks with one-command install across IDEs; currently free for developers and creators.

overview.text: AgenticMarket presents an ecosystem for MCP servers, reusable agent skills, model comparisons and the Andromity coding agent. It offers a CLI to install servers into supported editors and agent clients, with routing, authentication and execution through its infrastructure. Users can browse server listings and developers can publish servers. Its verification labels and benchmark scores are platform assessments.

platforms.name: Agents Trust
platforms.summary: Index that helps an agent choose a paid API for a task and check it before paying: it returns candidate endpoint URLs with price, reliability, delivery evidence and risk flags, through two paid x402 GET calls.

key_number.unit: calls in 30 days (CDP Bazaar quality data)

platforms.disclosure: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0), verified by Commonworld unpaid 402 probe 2026-10-23 (20:24-20:59 UTC). No payment, deal or contact with Agents Trust or YourAITools is involved.

overview.text: Agents Trust presents paid API discovery and recorded endpoint evidence before a separate direct purchase from a provider. Recommend lists 0.01 USDC per query; Inspect costs 1% of the endpoint's lowest quote with a 0.001 USDC floor. Only the exact normalized demo phrases weather, crypto prices and web search are advertised free. Endpoint scores, provider scores and provisional evidence tiers are separate, not endorsements or safety guarantees. Counts include its own URLs; payment activity inferred from settlements to advertised recipients does not prove purchase of an exact URL. A successful challenge is not a paid-delivery test, and delivery evidence does not establish content quality. Even live=1 can use stored probes or leave reachability unknown; the provider's current offer is authoritative. Base, Solana and Algorand payment rails are distinct from chains analyzed by an API. Hosted MCP is keyless and cannot pay or accept wallet keys. A response may precede settlement; existing-attempt receipt checks are separate from a new payment.

platforms.name: AgentStore (AgentPay)
platforms.summary: Marketplace where AI agents and people pay listed agent services per query in USDC on Base over x402; run by the team behind AgentWorld.

overview.text: AgentStore is AgentPay's marketplace for creating, renting and hiring AI agents. Its store page lists per-query agent services paid in USDC on Base through x402, alongside agent avatars and NFT minting. AgentPay also has a separate directory of agent-facing endpoints.

platforms.name: Alipay AI Pay / ACT
platforms.summary: Ant Group's AI-native payment product letting consumers pay through AI agents (Qwen App, Taobao Instant Commerce, OpenClaw-type agents), plus a business-side AI payment processing product.

overview.text: Ant Group's release presents Alipay AI Pay within a China-focused payment and merchant-services ecosystem. It describes a payment stack comprising AI Pay, AI Wallet, AI payment processing and Token Pay, supported by an Agentic Commerce Trust Protocol. It also describes connecting merchant AI agents to Alipay Tap! devices for operations analysis, marketing, membership management and commerce services.

platforms.name: Amazon Rufus / Buy for Me → Alexa for Shopping
platforms.summary: Amazon's in-store AI shopping assistant (renamed from Rufus to Alexa for Shopping on 13 May 2026) that can auto-buy and, via Buy for Me, purchase on other retailers' sites.

overview.text: Amazon presents Alexa for Shopping as its shopping assistant combining Rufus product expertise with Alexa+ personal context. Its official article describes product research and comparisons, price history and alerts, cart building and scheduled shopping actions. Shop Direct surfaces products from other stores; Buy for Me handles purchases for eligible products. Amazon says the assistant is free for signed-in customers and available in full in 13 countries, with beta access in the United Arab Emirates and Turkey. This overview describes the official article, not verified shopping functionality.

platforms.name: Apify Store
platforms.summary: Marketplace of ready-to-run scrapers/automations (Actors) callable by AI agents via API/MCP, where developers publish tools and earn pay-per-use revenue.

money_flow.statement: Operator: $1.7M paid out to developers last month
money_flow.window: 'last month' (likely Sep 2026; page dates up to 2026-09-24)

key_number.window: 'last month' (likely Sep 2026; page dates up to 2026-09-24)

overview.text: Apify Store is a marketplace of ready-to-run tools called Actors for web data, automation and AI integrations. Its homepage lists social-media and e-commerce scrapers, a maps scraper and a website content crawler. The platform offers hosted execution, API access, scheduling and integrations through MCP, CLI and Skills. Developers can publish Actors and earn from their use; running Actors can involve usage charges.

platforms.name: AsterPay
platforms.summary: EUR-native facilitator for AI agent payments: agents pay over x402 or MPP and the business receives euros in its bank via SEPA Instant; it also sells some data APIs per call over x402.

key_number.unit: calls in 30 days (CDP Bazaar quality data)

platforms.disclosure: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0), verified by Commonworld unpaid 402 probe 2026-10-23 (23:09-23:11 UTC). No payment, deal or contact with AsterPay or YourAITools is involved.

overview.text: AsterPay presents x402/MPP facilitation, agent-wallet trust scoring and stablecoin-to-EUR bank payouts. Its readiness checker and sample receipt are product interfaces/illustrations. EUR pricing is 0.5% plus EUR0.10, called per payout in the headline but per settled transaction in FAQ. Facilitation starts at EUR0.001/call with high-volume monthly plans; data APIs separately list $0.0015-$0.15 USDC/call. Free reads/keyless payments do not imply anonymous bank payout: production EUR settlement needs approved KYB and a bank account. Base, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum and Optimism support varies by token; EURCV is listed on Ethereum, EURC on Base/Ethereum. Lightning is separate; Solana, XRPL, Monad and GBP payouts are roadmap. The operator calls itself a technical provider using licensed European partners; MiCA-aligned is not independent licence verification. Speed/compliance claims and KYA scores do not guarantee identity, safety or refunds. Escrow thresholds conflict below 70 versus below 30. Privacy terms cover KYB/transaction records, immutable chain data, logs and human review of consequential automated decisions.

platforms.name: BAGS
platforms.summary: Lets developers sell APIs, tools and digital products to agents with USDC payment links and x402 pay-per-use access; agents hit an endpoint, see the price, pay and retry, with no buyer accounts and no API keys.

key_number.unit: calls in 30 days (CDP Bazaar quality data)

platforms.disclosure: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0), verified by Commonworld unpaid 402 probe 2026-10-23 (23:37-23:37 UTC). No payment, deal or contact with BAGS or YourAITools is involved.

overview.text: BAGS at getbags.app presents pay-per-request API commerce: sellers connect an API and set a price, compatible buyers receive a challenge, pay and retry, and BAGS says it forwards paid calls, delivers responses and credits seller balances after success. Public material describes x402 discovery, seller setup and wallet onboarding. Animated requests, prices and balances are explicitly simulations, not verified revenue or independent customer activity. Sandbox checks use test funds; live checks spend real USDC. Discovery eligibility follows a successful live settlement, not sandbox testing, and eligibility is not guaranteed discovery or sales. No-buyer-account/key language does not remove wallet funding, payment authorization or seller setup. Payment verification, delivery and payout claims are operator descriptions rather than independently tested outcomes. This BAGS service is distinct from the Bags token-launch service linked by Clawnch.

platforms.name: Basis Theory
platforms.summary: Basis Theory is a payment-tokenization vault that also issues scoped, single-purchase agentic payment credentials (Visa Intelligent Commerce, Mastercard Agent Pay, Stripe Shared Payment Tokens) so AI agents can pay without holding raw card data.

overview.text: Basis Theory presents a payment vault and bounded credentials for agent purchases. Its Agentic Payments documentation describes customer-approved allowances with amount, purpose, expiry and optional merchant, then scoped credentials rather than the underlying card. Network programs require customer verification; Stripe shared tokens have different enforcement. Access requires onboarding and provider eligibility. Minting permanently consumes allowance capacity even if unused or declined, and Basis Theory does not observe downstream settlement or refunds.

platforms.name: Catena Labs (ACK)
platforms.summary: Catena is a governance and banking platform for AI agents (Agent Commerce Kit open-source + Catena Trust Bank, which received OCC preliminary conditional approval on 18 Sep 2026).

overview.text: Catena presents financial infrastructure for businesses using agents: virtual dollar accounts or connections to existing financial partners, payment policies, approval escalation and transaction records. It describes dollar and stablecoin payments. Catena Assure offers reimbursement for qualifying control failures under program terms, eligibility, exclusions and limits; it is not insurance. Catena Labs is a financial technology company, not an FDIC-insured bank, and its planned bank is not yet open or offering services.

platforms.name: Circle Agent Stack + Arc
platforms.summary: Circle's agent toolkit (programmable USDC agent wallets, gas-free nanopayments via Gateway, CLI/skills, an Agent Marketplace) plus Arc, Circle's chain (mainnet 16 Sep 2026).

overview.text: Circle Agent Stack presents USDC infrastructure for agent wallets, service discovery and payments. Its components include Agent Marketplace with a Discovery API, policy-controlled Agent Wallets, Circle Skills, a CLI and Gateway-powered Nanopayments. Described controls include spending limits, per-service caps, allowlists and time-bounded sessions. It supports x402 on supported chains; its page lists Arc as testnet, with mainnet forthcoming. Circle states that it does not verify agent identity, safety or performance, and permitted transactions may occur without real-time human review.

platforms.name: Clawcard.sh
platforms.summary: CLI and API that give an AI agent an email address, a phone number, payment cards, a wallet, an onchain identity and access to paid APIs.

current_limitation.text: The hosting page returned HTTP 503 and an owner-paused deployment notice. A current product overview could not be confirmed.

platforms.name: ClawCredit
platforms.summary: Beta credit line for AI agents, underwritten by t54 according to the operator, spendable on x402 services and grown by repaying on time.

overview.text: ClawCredit presents a beta credit line for AI-agent spending on x402 services, underwritten by t54 according to the operator. It advertises XRPL, Solana and Base, an invite-code application, optional World ID verification and wallet-funding routes. Runtime identity, spending and repayment history are described as credit-decision inputs. Credit is borrowed spending capacity, not a free grant or guaranteed approval. Agent/pre-qualifying-node counts, cumulative payments and credit totals are publisher reports, not independently reconciled borrowers or settlements; repeated background payment rows are illustrations. Network and any-x402 claims do not guarantee endpoint acceptance. The documentation index describes Phase1 manual dashboard repayment alongside agent-wallet repayment promotion, leaving the applicable route unclear. Interest, fees, due dates, default consequences, recourse, jurisdiction and final loan terms are not established by those pages.

platforms.name: Clawnch
platforms.summary: Token infrastructure for AI agents on Robinhood Chain: agent-only token launches through signed launch tickets and Bags, plus an SDK and finance toolkit; the operator says launching agents earn trading fees.

overview.text: Clawnch presents token infrastructure for agents on Robinhood Chain, linking Clawncher launch/trading/liquidity tooling, Clawnchpad ecosystem tools and other launch-related products. Clawncher describes EIP-712 launch tickets bound to an agent wallet, deployment through Bags, creator-fee claims via API and programmatic trading/portfolio tools. These are financial-tool descriptions, not proven profit or payouts. Market-cap, fee, token and volume counters are operator aggregates rather than independently reconciled transactions or a forecast of agent earnings. Agent-only reverse-CAPTCHA authentication does not establish independent operators, safe software or reliable markets. The Bags token-launch route is distinct from BAGS API commerce at getbags.app. SDK/plugin/chat launch examples are setup descriptions, not evidence of completed launches, trades, liquidity provision or fee claims.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Pay Per Crawl / Monetization Gateway
platforms.summary: Cloudflare's Monetization Gateway lets sites and APIs behind Cloudflare charge AI agents per request using HTTP 402 (x402-compatible), alongside Pay Per Crawl/Pay Per Use for content; currently a closed beta for U.S.-based sellers and buyers.

overview.text: Cloudflare's September 2026 announcement presents Monetization Gateway as a closed beta for charging agents per request with HTTP 402. It covers websites, APIs, MCP tools and datasets, with seller-defined pricing and payment verification and settlement through Coinbase's x402 Facilitator using USDC on Base. The announcement limits beta access to eligible US-based sellers and buyers, and distinguishes this request-based product from Pay Per Use for reused content.

platforms.name: Coinbase AgentKit / Agentic Wallets
platforms.summary: Coinbase Developer Platform tools giving AI agents stablecoin wallets (awal CLI and MCP) with guardrails and native x402 payments; AgentKit is the open-source agent toolkit.

overview.text: Coinbase Wallet MCP connects AI assistants to wallet balances, transfers, swaps, contract interactions and x402 API payments. Its documentation distinguishes individual approval links for main-wallet actions from eligible dedicated agent wallets with expiring signing grants and saved spending controls. Autonomous actions depend on enabled tools, supported assets and networks, a shared rolling spending allowance and available gas; enrollment does not enable every action.

platforms.name: Coinbase CDP Facilitator + Bazaar
platforms.summary: Coinbase Developer Platform's x402 facilitator verifies and settles x402 payments; its Bazaar is a public catalog of payment-gated resources the facilitator has discovered.

money_flow.statement: x402-list on-chain measurement: Coinbase facilitator settled $767,328.44 over 30 d (2,628,442 settlements; $192,781.15 over the last 7 d), settlement to anyone (gross, not seller revenue)
x402stats: coinbase attributed seller volume $575,892 over 30 d, 34,288 sellers of which 69 pass the organic filter (>=$100, >=3 buyers).

overview.text: Coinbase documentation describes x402 Bazaar as a catalogue of payment-gated services discovered by the CDP Facilitator. Public discovery is available through SDK functions, REST APIs or Bazaar MCP without a CDP API key. Users can search by intent and filter by network, asset, payment scheme, merchant or maximum price, browse indexed resources or list a merchant's services. Search combines relevance with site-defined quality signals; discovering a service and paying for it are separate steps.

platforms.name: Crossmint
platforms.summary: Stablecoin infrastructure company offering wallets for users and AI agents, agentic virtual cards and agentic payments APIs.

overview.text: Crossmint presents infrastructure connecting fiat and stablecoins for embedded finance, treasury and payments. Its agentic-payments offering includes Agent Wallets, virtual cards with spending limits and merchant controls, Agent Checkout and Menta, an open-source commerce plugin. The site provides developer resources and sales-contact routes for agent products.

platforms.name: Daydreams (router + facilitator)
platforms.summary: Daydreams builds agent-commerce infrastructure: an x402 pay-per-inference LLM router, an open-source x402 facilitator, Lucid Agents SDK and Task Market; it has a $DREAMS token.

money_flow.statement: x402-list on-chain measurement: Daydreams facilitator settled $1,057.94 over 30 d (977 settlements; $16.03 over the last 7 d), settlement to anyone (gross, not seller revenue)

books.label: Open: its money figures are on a public dashboard or API

overview.text: Daydreams Systems presents commerce infrastructure for autonomous agents: markets, payment rails, routing and settlement. Task Market is described as funded briefs with USDC escrow, worker competition and payment for an accepted result, using bounty, claim, pitch, benchmark or auction modes. The homepage also presents Lucid Agents for building paid agent services, Dreams Router and agent-payment tooling.

platforms.name: Dexter / Indexter
platforms.summary: Dexter offers a self-custodial agent wallet with spending caps ('Tabs'), an x402 facilitator on eleven chains, and Indexter, a searchable catalog of paid services for agents.

money_flow.statement: x402-list on-chain measurement: Dexter facilitator settled $1,062.69 over 30 d (7,305 settlements; $0 over the last 7 d), settlement to anyone (gross, not seller revenue)
x402stats: dexter attributed seller volume $1,902 over 30 d, 57 sellers of which 2 pass the organic filter (>=$100, >=3 buyers).

books.label: Open: its money figures are on a public dashboard or API

overview.text: Dexter presents a self-custodial account for payments, credit and obligations involving people, companies and agents. It links OpenDexter for supported agent clients, Indexter for service discovery, Tabs for spending limits, Dexter Connect for sign-in and an x402 SDK. Indexter is described as showing providers, prices and expected results before payment. The homepage also offers a private-beta request, so it does not establish general availability of every account feature.

platforms.name: FluxA
platforms.summary: FluxA offers AI-agent payment infrastructure: an agent co-wallet with budgets/mandates, single-use AgentCards, AgentMarket discovery and AgentCharge for accepting USDC from agents.

money_flow.statement: x402-list on-chain measurement: FluxA facilitator settled $313,309.69 over 30 d (248,480 settlements; $157,930.92 over the last 7 d), settlement to anyone (gross, not seller revenue)
x402stats: fluxa attributed seller volume $321,401 over 30 d, 3,582 sellers of which 3 pass the organic filter (>=$100, >=3 buyers).

books.label: Open: its money figures are on a public dashboard or API

overview.text: FluxA presents agent-payment infrastructure spanning AgentWallet, single-use AgentCard, AgentMarket discovery, AgentCharge USDC acceptance and AI spending management. Its intent-based flow asks a user to approve a budget and purpose, with subsequent spending evaluated by a wallet risk engine. Payment Security is labelled beta. Its AEP2 description separates immediate off-chain mandate verification from later batched on-chain settlement.

platforms.name: Gondola
platforms.summary: Marketplace for Venice AI inference: holders of Venice DIEM deposit an inference key and set a price, and buyers call frontier models through one OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoint paid in USDC (also per call over x402); in beta.

key_number.unit: calls in 30 days (CDP Bazaar quality data)

platforms.disclosure: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0), verified by Commonworld unpaid 402 probe 2026-10-23 (20:24-20:59 UTC). No payment, deal or contact with Gondola or YourAITools is involved.

overview.text: Gondola presents a brokered inference marketplace where sellers supply Venice or Agent Zero API capacity and buyers pay metered USDC on Base. OpenAI/Anthropic compatibility and accountless access are endpoint-specific; video needs a key. Seller prices, routing within a band of the cheapest healthy capacity, referral preference and fallback to Gondola's key qualify cheapest-offer/discount marketing. Buyer and seller fees are each up to 2%; accountless x402 has a $0.01 minimum charge. Excess payment above metered cost remains wallet credit rather than an automatic cash refund; normal keys draw prepaid balance. Gondola's no-prompt-storage claim does not cover every upstream: privacy tiers differ, text may pass through Agent Zero, accounting metadata remains and video source clips above 18 MiB may be stored privately for a job. Privacy/spend caps are documented, not independently tested. A completed video job can be charged even if its clip is no longer downloadable. Advertised APR assumes full utilization and depends on demand, routing and pricing, not guaranteed yield or verified model provenance.

platforms.name: Google AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol)
platforms.summary: Open protocol, originated by Google and donated to the FIDO Alliance in April 2026, defining how agents, merchants and payment providers handle user-authorised agent payments.

overview.text: Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) presents an open protocol for agent commerce focused on authorization, authenticity, accountability and verifiable user intent. Its documentation links a specification, executive summary, examples, glossary and FAQ, with A2A and Universal Commerce Protocol integration materials. It describes signed checkout and payment mandates for transaction authority.

platforms.name: Google UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol)
platforms.summary: Open commerce protocol (Google, Shopify and partners) giving platforms, agents and businesses a common language for discovery and checkout.

overview.text: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) presents an open commerce protocol spanning product discovery, cart building, identity linking, checkout and order management. Its documentation describes REST and JSON-RPC transports with AP2, A2A and MCP support. It links specifications, core concepts, versioning, a roadmap and reference implementations for commerce across shopping, lodging and food.

platforms.name: Heurist facilitator
platforms.summary: Heurist's x402 facilitator (Base, Stable, ZKsync and others) offering OFAC screening and keyless integration.

money_flow.statement: x402-list on-chain measurement: Heurist facilitator settled $0 over 30 d (0 settlements; $0 over the last 7 d), settlement to anyone (gross, not seller revenue)

books.label: Open: its money figures are on a public dashboard or API

overview.text: Heurist Facilitator presents an x402 payment layer with v1 and v2 integration examples, documentation and settlement-statistics links. It advertises multi-network operation, no API-key requirement and screening of sanctioned addresses. A code generator offers chain, framework, payout-wallet and token settings. Real-time observability and auto-buyback are marked coming soon. Compliance and reliability statements are provider claims.

platforms.name: Kite AI
platforms.summary: Kite is an EVM chain and identity/payment layer for AI agents (Agent Passport, stablecoin settlement) with the KITE token; explorer at kitescan.ai.

overview.text: Kite presents a payment and settlement platform for agents, combining workflow interfaces, Passport controls and Kite Chain. Passport is described as setting budgets, permissions and scope, checking actions before payment, keeping an audit trail and allowing access revocation. Kite Chain is presented as a settlement layer with native stablecoins, EVM compatibility and cross-chain messaging. The site links developer resources and technical and MiCAR whitepapers.

platforms.name: Lightspark
platforms.summary: Lightspark provides a money-movement API (Grid Global Accounts, payouts, stablecoins, cards) and lets account holders give AI agents bounded, policy-enforced spending authority.

overview.text: Lightspark presents APIs for accounts, cards, payments and fiat or stablecoin money movement for platforms and agents. It describes agent accounts with balances and rules, global accounts, transfers and card-based agent checkout. Its footer says Lightspark is not a bank, exchange or asset custodian, and provides payment and card products through partners. It also states that the described funds at its named banking partners are not eligible for FDIC insurance.

platforms.name: Locus
platforms.summary: One account for an AI agent to use thousands of paid APIs and data sources, billed per call with no separate subscriptions or keys; Locus also offers USDC wallets with spending controls, and some of its API routes answer over x402.

key_number.unit: calls in 30 days (CDP Bazaar quality data)

platforms.disclosure: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0), verified by Commonworld unpaid 402 probe 2026-10-23 (23:09-23:11 UTC). No payment, deal or contact with Locus or YourAITools is involved.

overview.text: Locus presents prepaid access to third-party agent tools and customer-balance billing with a platform markup. Its 17,900-tool/75-provider claims and animated balances/margins are catalogue marketing and illustrations, not tested availability or transactions. Documentation separates this credit product from the older on-chain wallet. Pro requires no crypto wallet; prepaid balances pay providers including x402/MPP sellers. Plans list Free, Plus $20/month, Enterprise $200/month and Enterprise Plus $1,000/month, with included monthly credits absent, $20, $30 and $100 respectively. Included credits expire each billing period; purchased top-ups are separate. Free excludes customer billing and does not make provider calls free. Published tool prices are the same across plans; 1,000 credits per dollar is a denomination, not free calls. Customer billing/markup needs Enterprise. Self-serve pool funding starts at $5; hosted-top-up margins become payable after a default 30-day hold. Response-priced calls reserve/reconcile usage; live-priced calls use quote ceilings. No-charge failures are limited to before provider success; same-key retries are documented as duplicate-charge protection.

platforms.name: Mastercard Agent Pay (+ AP4M)
platforms.summary: Mastercard's agentic payments programme (agentic tokens bound to agents) plus Agent Pay for Machines (10 Jun 2026) for high-frequency machine-to-machine payments across cards, accounts and stablecoins.

overview.text: Mastercard Agent Pay presents payment infrastructure for agentic commerce. Its stated approach uses registered agents, Mastercard network tokens, data-exchange standards and authenticated user intent with explicit consent. Agent Pay for Machines is described as enabling devices and agents to initiate, authenticate and complete payments for users and businesses.

platforms.name: MCP Marketplace
platforms.summary: Curated, security-scanned marketplace of MCP servers with one-click install for AI clients, listing free and paid servers.

overview.text: MCP Marketplace presents a catalogue of servers for MCP-compatible assistants, with search, categories, popular listings and creator submission routes. Listings distinguish local and remote tools and display price labels, GitHub stars, install counts, security scores and user ratings across coding, browser automation, communication, finance and other categories. These changing metrics are operator-provided displays, not independent measurements or proof of endorsement by a named publisher. The homepage advertises security scanning and simple installation, but a displayed score does not establish scanner quality, package safety or permission to grant a server account or device access.

platforms.name: MCPize
platforms.summary: MCP server marketplace and hosting where developers publish/deploy servers and keep 80% of subscription revenue.

overview.text: MCPize presents a marketplace, hosting and monetization platform for MCP servers. It describes server discovery, a unified gateway, credentials and billing, usage tracking, cost alerts and observability. Publishers can deploy servers and offer subscriptions; the homepage advertises an 80% publisher revenue share and a free request allowance. Its quality grades and verification badges are platform assessments.

platforms.name: Meridian (mrdn)
platforms.summary: Meridian is an x402-paid inference router exposing 400+ models from several providers through one API, settling on 19 chains, partly via prepaid top-ups.

money_flow.statement: x402-list on-chain measurement: Meridian facilitator settled $49,114.19 over 30 d (1,701 settlements; $2,855.12 over the last 7 d), settlement to anyone (gross, not seller revenue)
x402stats: mrdn attributed seller volume $128,789 over 30 d, 14 sellers of which 7 pass the organic filter (>=$100, >=3 buyers).

books.label: Open: its money figures are on a public dashboard or API

overview.text: Meridian presents x402 payment infrastructure for agents, merchants and models, covering escrow, settlement, refunds, disputes and payouts. Its homepage links documentation, statistics and a command-centre sign-in. Availability varies by feature: the Kleros dispute-resolution notice says coming, arbitration is labelled in progress, and cross-chain and off-ramp panels carry coming-soon labels.

platforms.name: Meta Muse
platforms.summary: Meta's consumer personal AI agent (US launch 8 Sep 2026, app + WhatsApp) that can act across connected apps and check out via Stripe Link and Shop Pay, with PayPal announced.

overview.text: Muse presents a Meta personal agent for goals and tasks, including shopping, email and connected apps. Its public page advertises mobile, desktop and WhatsApp access, a persistent cloud computer and browser, action approvals and an audit trail. Users are offered app connections with controls over what the agent can see and do.

platforms.name: Microsoft Copilot Checkout
platforms.summary: In-chat checkout inside Microsoft Copilot (U.S.), letting shoppers buy from merchants via PayPal, Shopify and Stripe rails without leaving the conversation; merchants remain merchant of record.

overview.text: Microsoft presents Copilot Checkout as purchases inside Copilot while merchants remain merchant of record and use their existing payment, fraud, tax and fulfillment systems. Its page connects discovery to Microsoft Merchant Center feeds and Universal Commerce Protocol attributes, and points Shopify merchants to Shopify controls. Eligibility is stated for English-language merchants selling to US buyers in USD; the Merchant Center checkout setting is marked as a selected-customer pilot.

platforms.name: Natural
platforms.summary: Natural is a San Francisco fintech building payment primitives for AI agents (wallets, payments, cards, accounts, billing) exposed via API, SDK, CLI and MCP.

overview.text: Natural presents payment infrastructure for AI agents, including wallets, payments, transfers and developer access through MCP, CLI, SDK and API. The site also describes identity-linked agents, payment monitoring and managed disputes. Cards, credit, voice, billing and per-call charging are labelled as coming soon.

platforms.name: Nevermined
platforms.summary: Payments infrastructure for AI agents: delegated card/credit spending, metering and settlement across x402, MPP and A2A, plus a services catalog/router; fee 1–2% of settled volume.

overview.text: Nevermined presents agent payments controlled by a spending mandate, with limits on amount, purchase count and expiry, and a revocation option. It offers MCP and SDK/API connections, an AI Services Catalog and Nevermined Pay for card or cryptocurrency settlement; bank rails are described as forthcoming. Its free-start offering has separate paid service usage and merchant plans.

platforms.name: Open Standard $OUSD
platforms.summary: Open USD (OUSD) is a stablecoin from Open Standard (founded by Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe and Visa), issued by Bridge, positioned as shared payment infrastructure including programmatic agent payments.

overview.text: Open Standard presents Open USD (OUSD) as shared stablecoin infrastructure for businesses, including payments, financial institutions, marketplaces and agentic commerce. Its stated model combines revenue sharing with companies growing adoption, shared governance and reserve management. The homepage advertises an integration route and fee-free minting and redemption, and links geographic restrictions and prohibited uses.

platforms.name: PayAI
platforms.summary: Solana-first x402 facilitator that verifies and settles USDC micropayments across Solana and several EVM chains, with an ecosystem/discovery page.

money_flow.statement: x402-list on-chain measurement: PayAI facilitator settled $22,509.64 over 30 d (90,883 settlements; $3,269.12 over the last 7 d), settlement to anyone (gross, not seller revenue)
x402stats: payAI attributed seller volume $14,022 over 30 d, 1,107 sellers of which 12 pass the organic filter (>=$100, >=3 buyers).

books.label: Open: its money figures are on a public dashboard or API

overview.text: PayAI presents an x402 facilitator and agent-payments SDK for supported Solana and EVM networks. It distinguishes payment verification from settlement, with availability, timing and fees depending on the network and scheme. It offers an Echo Merchant for payment testing, while Payment Splitting and Token Gateway are marked coming soon. Its FAQ treats pending settlement as unresolved and says discovery listings do not prove current service availability or quality.

platforms.name: PayAPI Market
platforms.summary: Curated x402 API marketplace where providers list APIs free and keep 100% of per-call USDC payments on Base or Solana, with settlement-verified badges and an MCP endpoint.

overview.text: PayAPI Market presents an x402 marketplace where agents discover APIs and pay providers per request in USDC on networks offered by each listing. It advertises free listing, free catalogue search and a zero-percent platform share of each job. Its settlement-verified label is described as a paid test of a specific route with a published receipt, not verification of every route in a listing. Provider prices and verification claims are marketplace-reported.

platforms.name: PayLobster
platforms.summary: Former payments layer for AI agents on Base: USDC escrow between agents, onchain reputation and credit scoring, x402 paid calls and spending mandates, through an SDK, CLI and MCP tools. The site no longer serves the service (checked 2026-10-22).

keys.label: The operator says a smart contract holds the funds
keys.quote: escrow, reputation, and credit scoring — on-chain

platforms.name: Payman AI
platforms.summary: Payman AI deploys AI agents for banks and credit unions that execute real banking transactions (payments, transfers, account analysis) by voice or text under institution-set controls.

overview.text: Payman AI presents agentic banking for banks and credit unions, with agents working inside existing institutional systems. Its homepage describes conversational payments, transfers, savings and account analysis. Institution-set policies, approval steps, audit trails and a bank-controlled kill switch are presented as controls. The site offers a sales demo for financial institutions.

platforms.name: PayOS
platforms.summary: PayOS sells payments data APIs (card, bank, KYC/KYB) and an 'Agent Data' line with agentic tokens, a PayOS wallet and agent monetization/checkout for letting AI agents pay.

overview.text: PayOS presents payments data for the agentic economy, including card, bank, business, user and transaction signals. It works alongside existing payment processors rather than replacing a gateway or processor, and advertises self-serve, pay-per-use access. Its agentic product line lists agent tokens, wallets, monetization and catalogue/checkout, with examples covering account checks, merchant risk and retry decisions.

platforms.name: PayPal Agent Ready + Store Sync
platforms.summary: PayPal's agentic commerce services: Agent Ready (payments in AI platforms) and Store Sync (catalog and cart API so AI agents can buy from merchants; US buyers, USD, physical goods, limited access).

overview.text: PayPal Agentic Commerce Services presents Store Sync and Agent Wallet. Store Sync is described as sharing product catalogues with participating AI channels, managing carts and supporting post-purchase fulfillment; Agent Wallet enables agent checkout with PayPal. The page limits Purchase and Seller Protection to eligible transactions, with terms, exclusions and limitations.

platforms.name: Perplexity (PayPal checkout)
platforms.summary: Perplexity's free U.S. shopping experience with 'Instant Buy' in-chat checkout powered by PayPal, merchants remain merchant of record.

overview.text: Perplexity's November 2025 launch article describes conversational product discovery and instant checkout with PayPal. It presents contextual product cards and remembered shopping preferences, with retailers remaining merchant of record and handling returns and customer relationships. The dated launch offered free access to US users on desktop and web, with mobile apps then planned; it does not establish the present regional or device rollout.

platforms.name: Pocket Network
platforms.summary: Decentralized network where developers publish HTTP data services and get paid onchain per request by AI agents and MCP clients; its Agentic Portal lists the services agents can call, and paid calls go over x402.

key_number.unit: calls in 30 days (CDP Bazaar quality data)

platforms.disclosure: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0).

overview.text: Pocket Network presents data services that developers publish and agents pay to call, alongside public RPC access. Its homepage advertises 120 services, including rule-based address normalization and named-entity recognition as well as model-based reranking. Developers are offered service registration, supplier setup, testing and an acceptance audit, with prices set in compute units per request and on-chain metering described at a stable dollar value. Callers use HTTPS endpoints paid per call through x402 or MPP. These are product terms, not verified demand, earnings or professional validation of every listed service.

disclosure_history.text: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0), verified by Commonworld unpaid 402 probe 2026-10-23 (20:24-20:59 UTC). No payment, deal or contact with Pocket Network or YourAITools is involved.
disclosure_history.reason: Editorial separation of source/relationship disclosure from historical research and probe notes. No new visit, practical trial or independent verification is implied.

platforms.name: Polygon Facilitator
platforms.summary: Polygon's hosted x402 payment facilitator that verifies and settles stablecoin payments for x402-enabled APIs on Polygon.

money_flow.statement: x402-list on-chain measurement: Polygon facilitator settled $110,463.87 over 30 d (3,667,791 settlements; $44,400.36 over the last 7 d), settlement to anyone (gross, not seller revenue)

books.label: Open: its money figures are on a public dashboard or API

overview.text: Polygon's x402 documentation describes HTTP 402 Payment Required as a request-and-response flow for on-chain API, web-service and agent payments. It lists separate Polygon Mainnet and Amoy testnet facilitators, alongside other provider routes, and links integration guides, a wallet MCP tool and mainnet-address analytics. Mainnet and testnet are not interchangeable. A documented endpoint or provider listing does not establish a completed payment, free access, escrow protection or guaranteed provider availability.

platforms.name: Ramp (VIC B2B)
platforms.summary: Ramp's agent offering gives company AI agents an identity, owner, budget and approved payment methods, including single-use Agent Cards issued on Visa Intelligent Commerce, with finance-team controls.

overview.text: Ramp presents finance tools for companies using agents, including cards, expenses, bill payments, banking, travel and AI spending. It describes agent identity and ownership, budgets, human approvers, merchant restrictions, approved payment methods and audit trails through reconciliation. The site lists Agent Card checkout, MPP and x402 for payments, with API, MCP and CLI connection options.

platforms.name: Robinhood Chain
platforms.summary: Robinhood Chain is a permissionless Arbitrum-based Layer 2 for tokenized real-world assets that markets itself as purpose-built for AI agents; x402 facilitators (Dexter, Meridian) settle on it.

overview.text: Robinhood Chain is presented as a permissionless Layer 2 for financial services and tokenized real-world assets, developed on Arbitrum infrastructure. Its listed agent use cases include trading, swapping, lending and payments. The page distinguishes Stock Tokens from shares: they provide economic exposure without legal or beneficial rights in the underlying securities. Stock Tokens are unavailable in the US and restricted elsewhere, and carry investment-loss risk.

platforms.name: Shopify Agentic Storefronts + Catalog API
platforms.summary: Shopify feature, on by default for eligible stores, that syndicates merchants' products into AI channels such as ChatGPT, Google AI Mode/Gemini, Microsoft Copilot and Meta.

overview.text: Shopify agentic storefronts enables product discovery and purchases through AI channels, subject to store, catalogue, policy and channel requirements. Its help article distinguishes ChatGPT referrals to store checkout from activated Shopify-powered direct checkout in other channels. Eligible stores have agentic storefronts active by default, while Agentic-plan stores have different setup and direct checkout off by default. Use requires agreement to supplemental terms.

platforms.name: Skyfire (KYAPay)
platforms.summary: Skyfire provides 'Know Your Agent' identity and KYAPay tokens that bundle verified agent identity with payment intent, for buyer and seller agents.

overview.text: Skyfire presents an Agent Trust Stack for agent identity, access and checkout. Its Know Your Agent (KYA) tokens are described as binding platform, agent and human identities with user mandates. The offering includes an Agentic Wallet for cards, stablecoins and mandates, plus a Buy for Me purchase experience through websites and agentic commerce protocols.

platforms.name: Solana x402
platforms.summary: Solana Foundation's landing page promoting x402 on Solana, with ecosystem links (facilitators, SDKs, explorers).

overview.text: Solana's x402 page introduces internet-native payments for web services, APIs and content. It describes paying per access rather than creating a provider account or subscription, and links ecosystem projects, an explorer, documentation, templates and tools for payment-gated MCP servers. Its activity figures are site-reported statistics, not evidence that a particular service is available or suitable.

platforms.name: Sponge
platforms.summary: Wallets and accounts that let AI agents pay, invest and earn, plus a gateway for businesses to sell services to agents over x402 and MPP.

overview.text: Sponge presents agent accounts for holding, spending, investing and earning, plus a separate business gateway accepting x402 and MPP payments. It advertises wallet, bank-account, crypto, trading and developer integrations, not a tested deployment or universal feature compatibility. Its card is described as a Rain-issued credit card backed by digital-asset collateral, distinct from the crypto wallet, virtual accounts and other platform features. The Visa acceptance claim does not establish a particular merchant's or country's eligibility. The illustrated daily budget, per-transaction limit and allowed domains are not proof of enforcement across every route. Balances, earnings, transfers and trades on the homepage are examples, not verified results. The homepage does not establish fees, collateral/liquidation terms, custody, withdrawal, insurance, geographic eligibility or refund conditions.

platforms.name: StableDomains
platforms.summary: Agent-first domain registrar: an agent can search, buy, renew and manage real ICANN domain names over a REST API, an MCP server or x402, paying in USDC or USDT on several chains with no card; it also sells domain-drop data per call over x402 (USDC on Base, $0.01-$0.10) and runs a referral…
platforms.disclosure: Disclosure: suggested for the Atlas by the operator, Tim Johnson (StableDomains), in an email to Commonworld on 2026-10-29. No payment, deal or paid placement is involved, and the card does not depend on one.

overview.text: StableDomains presents domain registration and management paid with USDC, USDT or card, with guest checkout, API/MCP/x402 access and WHOIS privacy where the registry permits. It advertises 435 endings and first-year prices from $2.79. Sample .com pricing is $16.99 initially and on renewal; .icu is $2.79 initially and $39.19 on renewal. These are examples, not an available-name quote or final total, and card payment adds a fee. The described flow locks a quote for 60 minutes and starts registration after payment confirms; registration also creates renewal obligations.

disclosure_history.text: Disclosure: suggested for the Atlas by the operator, Tim Johnson (StableDomains), in an email to Commonworld on 2026-10-29. No payment, deal or paid placement is involved, and the card does not depend on one. Every value was re-checked read-only by the Atlas against the site's own pages, its live 402 answers, Coinbase's Bazaar and the MCP Registry.
disclosure_history.reason: Editorial separation of source/relationship disclosure from historical research and probe notes. No new visit, practical trial or independent verification is implied.

platforms.name: Stripe Agentic Commerce Suite + Shared Payment Tokens
platforms.summary: Stripe's merchant-side product suite (launched 11 Dec 2025) that lets businesses sell through multiple AI agents, using Shared Payment Tokens for agent-initiated payments.

overview.text: Stripe's agentic-commerce documentation groups integrations for agent builders and sellers. It covers Link Agent Wallet, embedded commerce, browser payments with WebMCP, retail checkout, service bookings, machine payments and scoped Shared Payment Tokens. The introduction says availability, launch stage and supported countries vary by integration.

platforms.name: Stripe Issuing for agents + Link agent wallet
platforms.summary: Stripe Link's wallet for agents, letting consumer AI agents (e.g. Meta Muse) pay with a user's saved Link methods or single-use virtual cards, with purchase protection.

overview.text: Stripe's article dated 29 September 2026 describes Link's wallet for consumer-agent purchases, including incremental authorization, guidance through checkout obstacles, consumer-permissioned financial insights and protections for eligible transactions. It names Muse as the first agent offering those purchase protections, with wider protection availability and future spending controls described as plans. The article distinguishes help completing approved purchases from proposed budget-based autonomy. These dated product statements do not establish present eligibility for every agent, country, merchant or transaction, and the protections are conditional rather than a blanket guarantee.

platforms.name: Tempo + MPP (Machine Payments Protocol)
platforms.summary: Tempo is a stablecoin-payments blockchain (mainnet 18 Mar 2026) and, with Stripe, co-author of MPP, an HTTP 402 protocol for charging agents per API call or tool use.

overview.text: Tempo presents a blockchain for stablecoin financial products. Its agentic-payments page describes Machine Payments Protocol (MPP) as a way for agents to pay for APIs, tools and services. The page advertises per-call or per-request pricing alongside subscriptions and prepaid credits, with links to MPP and developer resources.

platforms.name: Thirdweb x402
platforms.summary: thirdweb's x402 client/server SDKs and facilitator for accepting x402 payments on 170+ EVM chains.

money_flow.statement: x402-list on-chain measurement: Thirdweb facilitator settled $49.89 over 30 d (50 settlements; $13.45 over the last 7 d), settlement to anyone (gross, not seller revenue)

books.label: Open: its money figures are on a public dashboard or API

overview.text: thirdweb x402 Payments documentation describes client/server integration for paid APIs, websites and agents using HTTP 402. It provides client, server, agent, facilitator and Solana guides, plus a playground link. Its React client handles payment-required responses with wallet connection, funding and error UI; server examples check payment information before serving content. EVM payments require tokens supporting the documented permit or authorization standards.

platforms.name: Virtuals ACP
platforms.summary: Virtuals Protocol's Agent Commerce Protocol, an on-chain marketplace where agents hire other agents for jobs settled through escrow, now on v2 (ERC-8183 reference).

money_flow.statement: Independent on-chain: ACP v1 platform fee $345,197 in Mar 2026 vs $5.48 in Sep 2026; ACP v2 ~$2,660 stablecoin over six months

overview.text: Virtuals Agent Commerce Protocol provides a public Scan dashboard for agent commerce. It displays aggregate charts, ranked agent entries, service offerings, jobs and transaction records with explorer links. The interface also offers agent discovery, agent creation and login, with marketplace activity presented through platform-reported metrics.

platforms.name: Visa Intelligent Commerce + Trusted Agent Protocol
platforms.summary: Visa's agentic-commerce portfolio (tokenised credentials, controls, Trusted Agent Protocol) under which AI agents complete purchases; live in Europe since 2 Jul 2026 with 30+ issuers.

overview.text: Visa Intelligent Commerce presents a portfolio for agent-initiated transactions, covering payment credentials, controls, authentication and protections. Its public page describes Commercial Solutions, Intelligent Commerce Connect, a command-line interface and Trusted Agent Protocol. Visa says the product is still being deployed and its final version might not include every described feature.

platforms.name: Voidpay (Voidly)
platforms.summary: Voidly's marketplace of agent service storefronts: agents pay per call in USDC on Base after reading HTTP 402 terms, or prepare checkout links that the owner approves in a browser.

overview.text: Voidpay distinguishes wallet-enabled x402 calls, paid in USDC on Base under current payment terms, from hosted marketplace checkout reviewed by an owner in a browser. Hosted and local MCP are described as public-read and checkout-link transports that do not sign or pay. A separate local Wallet Kit has per-call and UTC-day limits for its own ledger, not every transaction from the wallet address. The saved catalog status is unavailable, and its Northstar Studio storefront is explicitly illustrative. Listings and seller admission do not establish live checkout or payouts; a transfer receipt alone does not prove delivery, quality or demand.

platforms.name: x402 Atlas
platforms.summary: Analytics and discovery site for x402 APIs on Base: tracks x402 servers, payments and trends, with sign-up for full access; it also sells paid x402 data calls. Not the same project as the Atlas card 402atlas (402atlas.com).

key_number.unit: calls in 30 days (CDP Bazaar quality data)

platforms.disclosure: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0).

overview.text: x402 Atlas offers API discovery and payment analytics, with Base marked supported and Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism and Solana coming soon despite broader multi-chain marketing. Its analytics panel shows ecosystem transactions, USDC value, buyers and providers, not customers of this analytics product or independently verified organic commerce. Promotional coverage and verification claims are not established by those displays. Free-account copy appears alongside a $49 Trial for 14 days, explicitly without a subscription, and custom-priced Premium; full-platform access is not established as free. This is x402atlas.com, distinct from 402atlas.com.

disclosure_history.text: Source: listed on YourAITools (youraitools.co, CC BY 4.0), verified by Commonworld unpaid 402 probe 2026-10-23 (20:24-20:59 UTC). No payment, deal or contact with x402 Atlas or YourAITools is involved.
disclosure_history.reason: Editorial separation of source/relationship disclosure from historical research and probe notes. No new visit, practical trial or independent verification is implied.

platforms.name: x402 Foundation
platforms.summary: The x402 Foundation (Linux Foundation project) stewards x402, an open standard that revives HTTP 402 so clients and agents can pay per request in stablecoins.

overview.text: x402 presents an open, neutral standard for internet-native payments between clients and servers. Its HTTP flow returns 402 Payment Required, lets a client pay and then retries the request to receive access. The site describes uses including API monetization, agentic commerce and paid content, with links to documentation, code and community resources. It states there are no protocol fees, while payment-network fees still apply.

platforms.name: x402-list
platforms.summary: Independent x402 directory that monitors listed services' uptime and pricing and meters their on-chain USDC settlement, with JSON API.

money_flow.statement: $326,934.95 paid to listed services over 30 d (11,129 buyers, 1,840,501 settlements), net of self-payments; largest single service 70.1%, top 10 services 95.4% (stats API traction block: a measured floor, not an ecosystem total)
money_flow.window: trailing 30d to the source's as-of time (x402-list traction.as_of, kept as source_as_of; it can lag our read)

money_flow.statement: All measured facilitators settled $2,625,294.37 to anyone over 30 d (the per-facilitator 30-day volumes listed on the facilitators page, summed by x402-list in its stats API across 41 measured facilitators; not deduplicated)

books.label: Open: its money figures are on a public dashboard or API

overview.text: x402 List presents a directory of APIs and services accepting x402 payments, with search, categories, facilitator links and machine-readable access through API, OpenAPI, text and MCP routes. It distinguishes listed, answering and payment-ready services and publishes its measurement method. Its documented agent flow separates discovery, an endpoint request, payment authorization and retry. Status, prices and payment volumes are directory-reported measurements.

platforms.name: YourAITools
platforms.summary: Directory of AI tools, APIs and agent services that accept crypto, mostly x402 per-call payments in USDC on Base and Solana; each listing gives protocol, networks, token, price per call and a dated note from the operator's own unpaid 402 probe, and the whole list is a public CC BY 4.0 JSON file…
platforms.disclosure: Disclosure: YourAITools is run by the youraitools.co team (its X account calls itself an AI agent built by a bot swarm), which also sells 24 x402 tools of its own, an x402-enable service, a Pro data feed, paid listing and ad placements, and earns affiliate fees; it proposed this card by email to Commonworld. No payment or deal is involved; every value was re-checked by the Atlas against the site, its public JSON and live 402 answers.

overview.text: YourAITools combines a directory advertised as 520 tools across 14 categories with 144-plus first-party kits and 24 operator-owned APIs. It discloses that its own tools pay its own wallet and are separate from independent listings. Directory order is alphabetical, paid placements are labelled and an optional Most used sort counts outbound clicks, not paid usage. Availability checks and trust scores do not establish output quality or security. Download refunds are conditional on a fault the team cannot fix; USDC-bought usage credits are nonrefundable, while unused card-paid credit has a separate 14-day refund policy with bonuses forfeited.
